title: Seed and cable panel baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with three cable panels separated by seed-stitch columns.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in DK on 4 mm needles with three eight-stitch cable panels separated by ten-stitch seed-stitch columns. The finer gauge makes the cables more detailed than aran-weight alternatives. About 275 g of DK.
sourceNotes: Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Cable Panels, describes a seed-and-cable arrangement as a standard baby blanket layout. Weldon's Practical Knitter, 10th series (1894), §Cable Stitch Nursery Pieces, gives a DK-weight version with seed stitch separators.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rows = 10 × 10 cm in seed stitch on 4 mm needles. Cable panels draw in by about 2 sts per panel.

glossaryTerms.definition: An arrangement in flat knitting where vertical cable columns are separated by seed-stitch columns of equal or wider width. The seed stitch lies flat and does not curl, providing a stable backdrop that makes the cable columns stand out. This combination eliminates the need for a separate border treatment.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 4 mm needles in a
seed-and-cable panel layout
, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long.

Single-panel construction; no seaming. Three eight-stitch cable panels are separated by ten-stitch seed-stitch columns, with ten-stitch seed borders at each side edge. The DK gauge produces smaller, more detailed cables than aran weight and a finer overall hand, suitable as a heirloom-quality gift blanket. Budget about 275 g (about 600 m / 655 yards) of DK. Buy in matched dye lots.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 275 g (about 600 m / 655 yards) of DK-weight yarn. A smooth plied DK in natural or solid colour shows the cables best.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 6 (to mark the three cable panel boundaries)

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rows to 10 cm in seed stitch on 4 mm needles. Each eight-stitch cable panel draws in by about 2 stitches relative to an equivalent seed stitch count. The cast-on of 168 stitches accounts for this.
At 20 stitches per 10 cm with 168 stitches, the blanket will be about 84 cm wide.
Stitches used

items.name: seed
items.qty: k1 p1 alternating; on return rows knit the purls and purl the knits

items.name: C4F
items.qty: sl2 to cable needle, hold front, k2, k2 from cable needle

items.name: C4B
items.qty: sl2 to cable needle, hold back, k2, k2 from cable needle

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 168 stitches: [10 seed] + [8 cable] + [10 seed] + [8 cable] + [10 seed] + [8 cable] + [10 seed] + adjustments = 168. Long-tail tail: (4 × 168) / 10 + 15 = 67.2 + 15 = 82 cm. Measure 95 cm. Place markers after stitches 10, 18, 28, 36, 46, and 54 from each edge to mark the cable panels.
Body
Non-cable RS rows: work seed stitch in each seed column, k8 in each cable panel.
Cable RS rows (every 8 rows, starting row 5): work seed stitch in each seed column, then [C4F, C4B] in each cable panel.
WS rows: work seed stitch in each seed column, p8 in each cable panel.
Continue until the blanket measures 90 cm. When you set this aside, note which row of the 8-row cycle you are on.
Stitch count check-ins

At row 135 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 168 stitches: seed panels total 128 sts, cable panels total 24 sts, plus 16 adjustment sts. Count within each zone. At row 268: count again before casting off.
Common faults

Seed stitch columns reverting to rib: on a WS row, the purl stitches in the seed section were knitted instead of purled. Read the stitch on the needle before working it: if the right side of the stitch shows a purl bump, knit it.
The three cable panels not aligning on the same rows: cable rows in the three panels must be worked on the same RS row. Mark all three cable columns simultaneously with the same row counter.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern: seed the seed columns, knit the cable panels. Use needles one size larger to keep the cast-off row elastic.
Finishing
Weave in both ends. A gentle wet block will open the seed stitch and show the cable more clearly.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash DK. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
From a three-panel seed-and-cable layout, try a full Aran blanket next. Replace the rope cables with honeycomb, bobble, and lattice panels. Keep the seed-stitch columns between them.
